English: Clay Lamp Stand
A simple, portable clay stand for butter lamps, signifying the first efforts to bring light and unity to the nomad encampment.
Oil Lamp Hut
A small, hide-covered hut dedicated to burning oil lamps for blessings, gathering families and boosting morale.
Butter Lamp Pavilion
A larger felt pavilion where many butter lamps are lit, serving as the heart of communal gatherings and prayers.
Wick Room
A sturdy wooden structure for lamp-wick storage and preparation, allowing longer ceremonies and larger gatherings.
Sanctified Hall
A sanctified, semi-permanent wooden hall where major rituals are held and holy relics are displayed among brilliant lamps.
Expanded Pavilion
A grand, multi-tent structure with detailed altars and lamp alcoves, drawing crowds from neighboring clans.
Priests Chamber
Private quarters for the spiritual leader, adorned with sacred lamps
French: a place for meditation, guidance, and ritual preparation.

English: Blessed Room
A stone-walled sanctum, built for hosting high ceremonies and storing relics, its lamps visible for miles at night.
Holy Lamp Hall
A resplendent, multi-tiered hall with gilded lamp niches and sacred thangkas, drawing pilgrims from across the steppe.
Tibetan Lamp Sanctuary
A monumental sanctuary atop a hill, its thousands of ever-burning lamps a beacon of unity and spiritual power over the Tibetan highlands.
